name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area flash PMI eased to 51.9 in October; Q3 GDP grew 0.4%
state: The HCOB euro-area flash composite PMI fell to 51.9 in October from September, below the 52.7 expected but still above 50 (S&P Global, 23 Oct). Eurostat's flash estimate on 30 Oct showed Q3 GDP up 0.4%, though French output contracted. Neither stagnation nor a sub-50 PMI is confirmed as of 4 Nov; the final October PMIs are due this week.
for_you: Euro-area activity is still growing but slowing. Firms exposed to energy costs and French demand face the most pressure.
rubric_hit: Composite PMI 51.9 > 50 and GDP positive = Normal

sources.title: S&P Global PMI — HCOB Eurozone PMI releases
FXStreet — Eurozone HCOB Composite PMI declines to 51.9 in October

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
